# Models & Agents
> **OpenAI releases mathematical results from an internal frontier model in a public GitHub repository with Lean formalizations and compute estimates.**

**What You Need to Know:** OpenAI published new mathematical results generated by a frontier model, along with Lean formalizations, reasoning summaries, and estimates that each result used roughly three hours of ChatGPT Pro compute. The release includes protocols for revisions and citations and follows guidance from the Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence at the Institute for Advanced Study. Watch the repository for additional formalizations and future model disclosures. The company is also funding workshops and conferences focused on understanding major AI-produced mathematical results.
---
### Top Story
OpenAI released a broad range of new mathematical results produced by an internal frontier model. The company is publishing the results in a GitHub repository that includes formalizations of many proofs in Lean, ten summaries of the model’s reasoning, estimations of compute spent, and statistics on attempted problems. The average result used the equivalent compute of roughly three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking. OpenAI consulted the independent Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence at the Institute for Advanced Study to develop release protocols and is funding workshops around major AI-produced results. The company states it is working to responsibly release the model that produced these results while continuing to evaluate internal frontier models on mathematics and other sciences. The repository will be updated with more formalizations as they become available, and additional details about how the results were obtained are included to promote transparency. Future releases will focus on improving paper quality through better citations, exposition, and presentation. Source: [openai.com](https://openai.com/index/sharing-ai-progress-in-mathematics/)
---
### Model Updates
**WavePrune restricts each RoPE channel to its first rotation period: arXiv NLP**
WavePrune removes position aliasing in Rotary Position Embedding by limiting each channel to its first rotation period. The method raises the HELMET score on four of five tested models without extra tuning, including an increase from 35.7 to 40.0 on Qwen3-8B. When pretraining from scratch, models using WavePrune achieve lower validation loss at extrapolated lengths. The approach induces fine-grained sparsity that hardware-aligned CUDA kernels exploit for 1.15x prefill and 1.24x decoding speedups over FlashAttention-2 at 32K context. The paper shows that RoPE’s periodic structure beyond the first rotation period is largely redundant. Source: [arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06963)

**Fiorillo v0.5 answers randomized trial questions with calibrated probabilities: arXiv NLP**
Fiorillo v0.5 is a 4-billion-parameter open model fine-tuned on Qwen3-4B-Base with low-rank adapters and a decision head for the Evidence Inference 2.0 task. On the test split of 1,218 prompts from 333 articles, it achieved an expected calibration error of 0.0168, macro-F1 of 0.9248, and log loss 0.1829 below Gemma 4 31B-it. The model was trained only on the 1,431 training articles whose licenses permit reuse. It was released under the Apache License 2.0 after passing four pre-registered criteria on the Open Science Framework. Source: [arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.07019)

**Component-level interventions reveal sparse refusal mechanisms in four open-weight models: arXiv NLP**
Refusal directions concentrate in sparse component mechanisms comprising 28 to 48 percent of upstream attention and MLP components while retaining 88 to 101 percent of steering effectiveness. Within those mechanisms, effective steering further concentrates in approximately 50 percent of residual stream dimensions, retaining 85 to 98 percent of baseline performance. The study decomposes refusal steering across four open-weight models and releases all code and raw experimental results on GitHub. Low capacity reduces causal effectiveness by 84 percent and low responsiveness by 95 percent. Source: [arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06903)

**Condition-anchored generative distillation stabilizes continual learning across language modeling objectives: arXiv NLP**
CAGD retains a small set of old prompts, uses a frozen previous model to reconstruct completions, and matches predictive distributions while learning the next task. On a 219M masked diffusion language model, the method reduced four-task final held-out loss from 2.927 to 1.114 in one task order and from 2.168 to 0.891 in reverse order. The same soft targets lowered final average loss by 0.055 over hard replay when teacher-generated support was identical. The approach was tested on fresh facts and natural instructions across SMDM and Qwen3. Source: [arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06940)
---
### Agent & Tool Developments
**SanSi turns a pre-trained looped language model into a typed decision model: arXiv NLP**
SanSi reads option probabilities after every loop and trains each loop with a proper scoring rule so one model serves budgets from one to eight loops. On 10,027 test decisions from 59 sources, it reached 72.0 percent accuracy, 13.5 points above a non-looped model of the same shape. On depth-controlled tasks, loops extend solvable depth beyond training depths where larger single-pass models fail. Used as a judge for policy optimization with reinforcement learning and no gold answers, SanSi raised the generator’s F1 by 7.7 points. Source: [arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.07730)

**ReFold compresses rendered context for long-horizon agents without discarding history: arXiv NLP**
ReFold removes two kinds of inter-turn redundancy by replacing earlier displayed content with stubs and folding completed turns into one-line notes. It reduces token consumption by up to 2.5x and halves KV-cache memory per session across five long-horizon benchmarks and two frontier LLMs. Under capped context budgets, it avoids up to 92 percent of forced compactions. Under concurrent serving workloads, it reduces request queuing delays by up to 100 percent and accelerates inference by up to 1.7x while cutting inference costs by up to 3.4x. Source: [arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.07863)

**DLoop performs multiple drafting stages before verification in speculative decoding: arXiv NLP**
DLoop continues drafting while the draft model remains confident and verifies all accumulated tokens together. Loop-aware training exposes the draft model to its own hidden states for unverified tokens. Across EAGLE-3, DFlash, Domino, DSpark, and multi-token prediction modules, DLoop improves wall-clock speedup by 5 to 41 percent while preserving lossless decoding. Source: [arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.07659)
---
### Practical & Community
**Kurate assesses study quality across 4,347 papers using linked evidence passages: arXiv NLP**
Kurate scores papers on eight dimensions including statistical power, causal identification, preregistration, and conflict of interest. On 60 held-out clinical-trial documents, extracted information matched expert labels in 221 of 242 protocol scorepoints and 294 of 370 results-publication scorepoints. The system links each judgment to the specific passage supporting it and was applied to a corpus containing 3,913 randomized trial reports. Source: [arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.07306)

**TIDE 2.0 provides keyed de-identification for clinical notes with interval-preserving date shifts: arXiv NLP**
TIDE 2.0 runs an interchangeable recognizer and a keyed anonymizer on institution-owned hardware. Dates receive a per-patient, interval-preserving offset, and each value receives the same surrogate across all occurrences under a given key. On two gold-annotated corpora, the default configuration reached span-level recall of 0.88 in-domain and 0.77 on an out-of-domain corpus at precision 0.88 and 0.87. The engine is MIT-licensed and the recognizer is available under a gated research-use agreement. Source: [arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.07224)

**CroissantMiner benchmarks end-to-end extraction of Croissant dataset metadata: arXiv NLP**
The benchmark comprises 602 papers, 102 with human-validated gold annotations and 500 with LLM-generated silver annotations covering the full Croissant schema including Responsible AI fields. Single-pass extraction consistently outperformed four agentic architectures, with the largest gap on long-form RAI fields. The authors release the benchmark, evaluation code, judge audit, live demo, and leaderboard. Source: [arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.07132)

**AccentCL enables class-incremental accent classification robust to imbalance and domain shift: arXiv NLP**
AccentCL extracts multi-layer representations from a frozen Whisper-Large-v3 encoder and applies an imbalance-aware cross-entropy loss plus domain mean alignment loss. On a five-class task it achieved 77.1 percent balanced accuracy and 76.9 percent macro-averaged F1. Adding Spanish-accented English yielded 83.3 percent F1 on the new class while retaining 77.3 percent balanced accuracy on base classes; subsequent addition of Chinese-accented English yielded 61.8 percent F1 on the new class while preserving 77.6 percent balanced accuracy. Source: [arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.07426)
---
### Under the Hood: Frontier Model Result Sharing
Frontier labs now face a concrete choice when releasing scientific outputs from internal models: publish raw results with minimal supporting material or invest in verifiable artifacts that the broader community can check. OpenAI chose the second path by shipping Lean formalizations alongside the proofs, which lets any researcher run an automated checker rather than trust textual claims. The approach adds engineering overhead because the model must produce both a human-readable proof and a machine-checkable formalization, yet it removes the common failure mode where a claimed result later turns out to contain subtle gaps. Compute accounting is also supplied in the form of ChatGPT Pro hour equivalents, giving outsiders a rough sense of the inference budget without exposing proprietary training details. The repository design further includes explicit revision and citation protocols, which reduces the risk that later corrections become untraceable. Teams evaluating similar releases should weigh the extra formalization cost against the gain in external scrutiny; when the goal is accelerating collective progress rather than claiming priority, the verifiable route appears to be the current practical standard.
